hpi_details: frequent sneezing, runny nose with clear discharge, nasal congestion, and red, itchy, watery eyes. Worse when outdoors or on high pollen days. No sore throat, no cough, no fever, no shortness of breath. Symptoms occur every year around spring/summer.
ideas: thinks it is hay fever (seasonal allergic rhinitis) acting up again
concerns: worried because he cannot focus at work due to constant sneezing, and antihistamines make him too drowsy
expectations: wants advice on non-drowsy medication options and practical ways to avoid pollen
medications: tried over-the-counter cetirizine, but it makes him sleepy
social_hx: accountant, works in an office, non-smoker, has a pet cat (no symptoms around cat)

clinical_knowledge.topic: Sneezing and itchy, watery eyes for the past two weeks evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Sneezing and itchy, watery eyes for the past two weeks is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.

Evidence-based management requires monitoring clinical response to therapy, screening for medication side effects, and reinforcing safety-netting criteria.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Sneezing and itchy, watery eyes for the past two weeks.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
management_principles: Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
Provide clear patient education, address patient concerns, and establish explicit follow-up and safety-netting instructions.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Identify characteristic symptoms of allergic rhinitis (clear rhinorrhea, sneezing, conjunctival injection)
Differentiate allergies from viral upper respiratory infections (lack of fever/sore throat, seasonal recurrence)
Discuss treatment options, explaining that second-generation antihistamines are generally less sedating but can still cause drowsiness
Provide practical pollen avoidance strategies in simple English
suggested_questions: What kind of symptoms are you experiencing in your nose and eyes?
Do you have a fever, a sore throat, or a cough?
Have you had symptoms like this before at this time of year?
How are these symptoms affecting your daily life or work?
Which medication did you try, and how did it affect you?
Do you spend a lot of time outdoors, or have pets at home?

objective_cues.objective: Identify characteristic symptoms of allergic rhinitis (clear rhinorrhea, sneezing, conjunctival injection)

objective_cues.objective: Differentiate allergies from viral upper respiratory infections (lack of fever/sore throat, seasonal recurrence)
objective_cues.say: Any fever or sore throat, or does this come back the same time each year?

objective_cues.objective: Discuss treatment options, explaining that second-generation antihistamines are generally less sedating but can still cause drowsiness
objective_cues.say: Some antihistamines are less likely to make you sleepy, but any of them can affect some people, so check how you respond before driving.

objective_cues.objective: Provide practical pollen avoidance strategies in simple English
objective_cues.say: On high-pollen days, keep windows shut and shower after being outside.
